page.title: AI Transformation: From Pilots to Production | Vitalos
page.description: Move from scattered AI pilots to governed, production AI with measurable value: the right use cases, ready data, managed risk and workflow integration.

@graph.name: AI Transformation
@graph.description: AI value depends on the right use cases, ready data, governed risk, real workflow integration and reliable production. Leadership wants measurable results but lacks a safe, prioritised route to production.

mainEntity.name: Do we have to start with an assessment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Where data or readiness is uncertain, an AI Opportunity Assessment is the responsible start, because it tests feasibility, quality and risk before you commit to production. If the use case is already clear and the data is understood, we can move to a prototype.

mainEntity.name: Will a successful prototype go straight into production?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Prototype evidence does not automatically mean production readiness. Production AI needs evaluation, monitoring, security and human-oversight decisions appropriate to the use case, and prototype work does not include production hardening unless that is agreed.

mainEntity.name: Are you tied to one AI model provider?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We stay pragmatic about technology and vendors, and we make operational cost, reliability and provider dependence part of the design rather than an afterthought.

mainEntity.name: How are model, API and cloud usage costs handled?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usage costs are kept visible: they are separated from professional fees or capped by agreement, so a technically successful system does not become an unexpected cost.

mainEntity.name: Will you be able to tell us where our data goes?

acceptedAnswer.text: That is the aim: Vitalos should be able to answer which model or provider processes your data, whether it is used for provider training, where it is stored, what retention applies, what tools and permissions an agent has, how outputs are evaluated and what happens when the model fails.

page.title: Business Process Modernisation | Vitalos
page.description: Redesign manual, slow or fragmented workflows, then automate and integrate them, so critical processes no longer run on spreadsheets, re-keying and email.

@graph.name: Business Process Modernisation
@graph.description: Manual, slow or fragmented workflows create cost, delay and risk. When critical processes run on spreadsheets, re-keying and email, operations hold back growth and service quality.

mainEntity.name: Is this just buying automation software?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The work starts with how the process should run. Software, integration and automation follow the redesign, so the result is a better workflow rather than a faster version of the old one.

mainEntity.name: Do you replace our existing systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only where replacement is the right answer. Often the bigger gain comes from connecting the platforms you already have so information flows automatically between them.

mainEntity.name: Where does AI fit?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI is combined with deterministic workflow automation and software integration where it creates measurable value. Bounded, measurable workflows come first.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the process after go-live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ownership after the engagement is made explicit before it ends. Your team can take over with documented handover, or Vitalos can continue to operate and improve the workflow under a defined service.

page.title: Legacy Application Modernisation | Vitalos
page.description: Modernise ageing applications in controlled stages: assess, re-architect and progressively modernise legacy software, then operate it reliably.

@graph.name: Application Modernisation
@graph.description: Ageing applications and architecture constrain growth, reliability and the speed of change. They are expensive to maintain, risky to alter and hard to integrate with the rest of the business.

mainEntity.name: Do we have to replace everything at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Modernisation can replace, re-platform or progressively refactor parts of the system in stages, chosen by risk and value.

mainEntity.name: Why start with an assessment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Material legacy complexity is one of the cases where going straight to build is risky. An assessment establishes the architecture, dependencies and migration constraints first.

mainEntity.name: Who supports the system during and after modernisation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Responsibility is explicit at every stage. After transition, your team can take over with documented handover or Vitalos can operate it under Application Care.

mainEntity.name: Can you modernise a system another supplier built?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. For an inherited system the assessment also covers ownership and access, code and quality, security, data, operations and documentation before Vitalos commits to a plan or a service.

page.title: Data & Intelligence Transformation | Vitalos
page.description: Connect, clean, model and govern fragmented data, then build the reporting, operational intelligence and AI capability that decisions depend on.

@graph.name: Data & Intelligence Transformation
@graph.description: Data exists across several systems but is fragmented, low-confidence or difficult to turn into decisions. Management lacks reliable operational intelligence, and the data is not ready to support AI.

mainEntity.name: Do we need a new data platform?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. The assessment shows whether connecting and governing existing sources is enough, or whether a new platform is justified.

mainEntity.name: Is this preparation for AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often. AI adoption depends on data foundations, governance and systems integration. Good reporting is valuable in its own right, and it is also the base that later AI work builds on.

mainEntity.name: How do you handle data quality and ownership?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each important source gets an owner, lineage and quality expectations, and key metrics get documented definitions, so reports can be traced back to their data.

mainEntity.name: Where does AI come in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once the foundation can be trusted, advanced analytics or AI can be built on it, under the same evaluation, monitoring and governance controls as any other production AI.

page.title: Technology Recovery & Reliability | Vitalos
page.description: Triage an unstable, slow or unfinished critical platform, even one another supplier built: set a known baseline, stabilise, remediate and keep it reliable.

@graph.name: Technology Recovery & Reliability
@graph.description: A critical platform is unstable, slow or unfinished. It may have been built by another supplier, documentation may be thin, and the business depends on it working.

mainEntity.name: Will you take over a system another supplier built?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, after an assessment. Acceptance is never automatic: we need to understand architecture, code ownership, dependencies, security, deployment, data responsibilities, known incidents and documentation first.

mainEntity.name: Can you guarantee the system will be fixed?

acceptedAnswer.text: We do not promise outcomes before the assessment. It establishes what is wrong and what recovery involves, and it can conclude that a rescue is needed before any service starts, or that responsible support is not possible.

mainEntity.name: What if the right answer is to rebuild?

acceptedAnswer.text: Then the assessment says so. Recovery, modernisation and replacement are all legitimate outcomes, chosen on evidence.

mainEntity.name: What happens once the system is stable?

acceptedAnswer.text: It moves into managed engineering or application care within a defined service boundary, or back to your own team with documented handover.
